exam_set.title: Practice Set 2
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 10, Practice Set 2

questions.jp: TCP及びUDPのプロトコル処理において、通信相手のアプリケーションを識別するために使用されるものはどれか。
questions.romaji: TCP oyobi UDP no purotokoru shori ni oite, tsūshin aite no apurikēshon o shikibetsu suru tame ni shiyō sareru mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: In TCP and UDP processing, what identifies the peer application?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
IP finds the host; a port number finds the app door on that host.

Technical breakdown:
TCP and UDP headers carry source and destination port numbers. The destination port identifies the receiving application/service, while the tuple of addresses and ports identifies a communication endpoint.

Japanese keywords to remember:
ポート番号 = pōto bangō = port number
識別 = shikibetsu = identification

Why the best solution works:
エ identifies the application endpoint used by TCP or UDP.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
A MAC address identifies a network interface on a local data-link network.
イ:
A TCP sequence number orders byte-stream data; it does not identify an app.
ウ:
An IP protocol number identifies TCP, UDP, or another upper-layer protocol, not the application.

Memory trick:
Host = IP; app = port.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: ネットワーク機器に付けられているMACアドレスの構成として、適切な組合せはどれか。
questions.romaji: Nettowāku kiki ni tsukerarete iru MAC adoresu no kōsei to shite, tekisetsu na kumiawase wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which is the correct composition of a MAC address assigned to network equipment?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 先頭24ビット：エリアID、後続24ビット：IPアドレス
options.romaji: Sentō 24 bitto: eria ID, kōzoku 24 bitto: IP adoresu
options.en: First 24 bits: area ID; last 24 bits: IP address

options.label: イ
options.jp: 先頭24ビット：エリアID、後続24ビット：固有製造番号
options.romaji: Sentō 24 bitto: eria ID, kōzoku 24 bitto: koyū seizō bangō
options.en: First 24 bits: area ID; last 24 bits: unique manufacturing number

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 先頭24ビット：OUI（ベンダーID）、後続24ビット：IPアドレス
options.romaji: Sentō 24 bitto: OUI (bendā ID), kōzoku 24 bitto: IP adoresu
options.en: First 24 bits: OUI (vendor ID); last 24 bits: IP address

options.label: エ
options.jp: 先頭24ビット：OUI（ベンダーID）、後続24ビット：固有製造番号
options.romaji: Sentō 24 bitto: OUI (bendā ID), kōzoku 24 bitto: koyū seizō bangō
options.en: First 24 bits: OUI (vendor ID); last 24 bits: unique manufacturing number

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A standard 48-bit MAC address has a maker half and a device-specific half.

Technical breakdown:
The first 24 bits are the IEEE-assigned OUI identifying the organization/vendor. The following 24 bits are assigned by that organization to uniquely identify the interface. IP address and area ID are not these MAC fields.

Japanese keywords to remember:
先頭24ビット = sentō 24 bitto = first 24 bits
固有製造番号 = koyū seizō bangō = unique manufacturing number

Why the best solution works:
エ correctly pairs OUI with the vendor-assigned unique portion.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Neither area ID nor IP address forms the standard split.
イ:
The latter half is plausible, but the first half is OUI, not area ID.
ウ:
The first half is correct, but the latter half is not an IP address.

Memory trick:
MAC 48 = OUI 24 + device 24.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp:
次のIPアドレスとサブネットマスクをもつPCがある。このPCのネットワークアドレスとして、適切なものはどれか。

IPアドレス：10.170.70.19
サブネットマスク：255.255.255.240
questions.romaji: Tsugi no IP adoresu to sabunetto masuku o motsu PC ga aru. Kono PC no nettowāku adoresu to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka. IP adoresu: 10.170.70.19. Sabunetto masuku: 255.255.255.240.
questions.en: A PC has IP address 10.170.70.19 and subnet mask 255.255.255.240. What is its network address?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A /28 subnet comes in blocks of 16. Address 19 belongs to block 16–31.

Technical breakdown:
255.255.255.240 = /28, leaving 4 host bits. Block size = 256 − 240 = 16. Last-octet ranges are 0–15, 16–31, and so on. 19 lies in 16–31; applying IP AND mask gives network address 10.170.70.16.

Japanese keywords to remember:
サブネットマスク = sabunetto masuku = subnet mask
ネットワークアドレス = nettowāku adoresu = network address

Why the best solution works:
イ is the first address of the /28 block containing host 19.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
.0 is the previous /28 network.
ウ:
.31 is this subnet's broadcast address.
エ:
.255 is not the network address of the given /28 subnet.

Memory trick:
/28 → block size 16.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 2台のPCにIPv4アドレスを割り振りたい。サブネットマスクが255.255.255.240のとき、両PCのIPv4アドレスが同一サブネットに所属する組合せはどれか。
questions.romaji: 2-dai no PC ni IPv4 adoresu o warifuritai. Sabunetto masuku ga 255.255.255.240 no toki, ryō PC no IPv4 adoresu ga dōitsu sabunetto ni shozoku suru kumiawase wa dore ka.
questions.en: With subnet mask 255.255.255.240, which pair of IPv4 addresses belongs to the same subnet?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
/28 divides addresses into groups of 16. Both addresses must be inside the same group.

Technical breakdown:
Mask 255.255.255.240 is /28; block size is 16. Usable hosts in subnet 16–31 are .17 through .30. Both .17 and .29 are usable hosts in that subnet. Each other pair crosses a boundary at 16, 32, or 48.

Japanese keywords to remember:
同一サブネット = dōitsu sabunetto = same subnet
割り振る = warifuru = assign

Why the best solution works:
イ contains two usable addresses whose network address is 192.168.1.16.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
.14 is in 0–15; .17 is in 16–31.
ウ:
.29 is in 16–31; .33 is in 32–47.
エ:
.33 is in 32–47; .49 is in 48–63.

Memory trick:
/28 boundaries: 0, 16, 32, 48.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp:
次のネットワークアドレスとサブネットマスクをもつネットワークがある。このネットワークをあるPCが利用する場合、そのPCに割り振ってはいけないIPアドレスはどれか。

ネットワークアドレス：200.170.70.16
サブネットマスク：255.255.255.240
questions.romaji: Tsugi no nettowāku adoresu to sabunetto masuku o motsu nettowāku ga aru. Kono nettowāku o aru PC ga riyō suru baai, sono PC ni warifutte wa ikenai IP adoresu wa dore ka. Nettowāku adoresu: 200.170.70.16. Sabunetto masuku: 255.255.255.240.
questions.en: For network 200.170.70.16 with mask 255.255.255.240, which IP address must not be assigned to a PC?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
In each subnet, first address names the network and last address broadcasts to everyone. Neither belongs to a PC.

Technical breakdown:
A /28 block has 16 addresses. Network .16 spans .16–.31. .16 is network address, .31 is broadcast, and usable host addresses are .17–.30. Therefore .31 cannot be assigned to the PC.

Japanese keywords to remember:
割り振ってはいけない = warifutte wa ikenai = must not assign
ブロードキャストアドレス = burōdokyasuto adoresu = broadcast address

Why the best solution works:
エ is the all-host-bits-one broadcast address.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
.17 is a valid host address.
イ:
.20 is a valid host address.
ウ:
.30 is the last valid host address.

Memory trick:
Subnet first = network; last = broadcast.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: 192.168.0.0/23（サブネットマスク255.255.254.0）のIPv4ネットワークにおいて、ホストとして使用できるアドレスの個数の上限はどれか。
questions.romaji: 192.168.0.0/23 (sabunetto masuku 255.255.254.0) no IPv4 nettowāku ni oite, hosuto to shite shiyō dekiru adoresu no kosū no jōgen wa dore ka.
questions.en: In IPv4 network 192.168.0.0/23 (mask 255.255.254.0), what is the maximum number of usable host addresses?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
/23 leaves 9 host bits: 512 patterns, minus network and broadcast.

Technical breakdown:
Host bits = 32 − 23 = 9. Total addresses = 2^9 = 512. Traditional IPv4 subnet host capacity excludes all-zero network address and all-one broadcast address: 512 − 2 = 510 hosts.

Japanese keywords to remember:
個数の上限 = kosū no jōgen = maximum count
ホスト = hosuto = host

Why the best solution works:
エ is 2^(32−23)−2 = 510.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
23 is the prefix length, not host count.
イ:
24 is neither the host-bit count nor capacity.
ウ:
254 is the usable count for /24, not /23.

Memory trick:
IPv4 hosts = 2^(host bits) − 2.

Correct answer: エ
